business.body: Kriti Nutrients Limited sells branded cooking oils — Kriti-branded soybean oil, groundnut oil and mustard oil — built on a long-standing reputation for product quality and consumer/trade trust across Central India. Alongside the branded consumer business, the Company has an institutional export business and is building out value-added, protein-based food and feed ingredients drawing on its soybean-processing base, as part of a stated shift from a single-category edible-oil business toward a broader diversified foods organisation.

outlook.body:
- Widen distribution footprint, deepen retail penetration and strengthen dealer/distributor channel partnerships, with geographic expansion prioritised across Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan.
- Use AI-enabled sales and distribution management to sharpen planning, field execution and decision-making across the supply chain (last-mile distribution positioned as the next competitive battleground).
- Continue investing in automation, process optimisation and manufacturing capacity enhancement as a standing operating commitment rather than periodic upgrades.
- Deepen export market access and international customer relationships, underpinned by quality/compliance investment and a growing portfolio of value-added soybean ingredients.
- For FY26 the Board declared and paid an interim dividend of 300% (₹3 per ₹1 share), which it treated as the full and final dividend for the year, explicitly stating no further dividend was recommended 'to conserve the accumulated resources for the business purposes' — signalling a bias toward reinvestment and balance-sheet conservation over incremental payout. ₹400 Lakhs was transferred to general reserves during the year, consistent with continued reserve-building alongside dividend distribution. The Company also confirmed it has not accepted public deposits or loans in contravention of the Companies Act, indicating conservative external-funding practice.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The AR does not disclose a discrete new-plant or capacity-addition project with a commissioning timeline. FY26 expansion activity is described as ongoing manufacturing modernisation at the existing facility: commissioning of a fully automated pouch filling machine that cut packaging turnaround from 12 hours to under 8 hours, roughly a 15% improvement in lecithin capacity utilisation through process optimisation, and introduction of 15+ new SKUs across pouch and bottle formats. Management characterises further investment in automation, process optimisation and capacity enhancement as a 'standing commitment' rather than a one-off project, with overall capacity utilisation at 72% in FY26 against a stated target of 85% for FY 2026-27. Separately, members approved (EGM, 20th March 2026) an amendment to the Memorandum/Articles of Association inserting an ancillary object clause enabling entry into power generation (thermal, nuclear, solar), made on the directions of Madhya Pradesh Power Transmission Company Limited (MPPTCL) — an enabling corporate-law step with no named project, site or capex quantum disclosed.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Rising disposable incomes, greater health awareness, increasing demand for packaged/branded oils, a robust food-processing sector and government initiatives such as the National Mission on Edible Oils are cited as demand drivers for the Indian edible-oil market, projected to grow from 25.33 Million tonnes (2025) to 28.34 Million tonnes by 2034.
- India remains significantly import-dependent for edible oil — imports are expected to meet nearly 60% of domestic demand in 2025-26 (IVPA), with soybean oil sourced mainly from Argentina/Brazil and palm oil from Malaysia/Indonesia — a structural exposure to global supply and price volatility.
- Expansion of organised retail and e-commerce is cited as improving product accessibility across urban and rural markets, supporting the branded-oil growth mix.
- India's food processing industry (7.7% of manufacturing output, projected to reach roughly ₹47,13,350 Cr / US$535 Billion by end FY26) is expected to keep growing on rising consumption, exports and Make-in-India-linked support, with AI-based automation and smart packaging flagged as sector-transforming technology trends.
- Management frames broader Indian GDP growth (7.7% in FY26, expected around 6.6% in FY27) supported by resilient domestic consumption, investment activity and policy support as a macro tailwind for consumption-linked demand.
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers
